- The calculation of `miter->__remaining` was modified to reflect the new logic for `sg_pgoffset` and `__offset`.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The modifications in `lib/scatterlist.c` are interrelated as they collectively address the issue of handling cases where `sg->offset` exceeds `PAGE_SIZE`. The changes to `__offset` and `sg_pgoffset` ensure that the mapping iterator correctly calculates the remaining bytes to be processed, preventing failures in data copying due to offsets that exceed the mapped area. This patch effectively fixes the bug by maintaining the integrity of the mapping iterator logic, ensuring it operates correctly even when `sg->offset` is greater than `PAGE_SIZE`.

You will be given the root cause of a bug, the commit message and the corresponding patch.
        You need to extract all code statements that lead to the bug from the patch, based on the root cause and the commit message.

        Root cause:
        The bug occurs because the mapping iterator logic incorrectly assumes that the `sg->offset` will always be less than `PAGE_SIZE`. When `sg->offset` exceeds `PAGE_SIZE`, it leads to incorrect calculations in the mapping iterator, causing `sg_copy_to_buffer()` to fail as it attempts to access data outside the kmapped area, resulting in improper data copying.
        
        Commit message:
        lib/scatterlist: Fix mapping iterator when sg->offset is
 greater than PAGE_SIZE

All mapping iterator logic is based on the assumption that sg->offset
is always lower than PAGE_SIZE.

But there are situations where sg->offset is such that the SG item
is on the second page. In that case sg_copy_to_buffer() fails
properly copying the data into the buffer. One of the reason is
that the data will be outside the kmapped area used to access that
data.

This patch fixes the issue by adjusting the mapping iterator
offset and pgoffset fields such that offset is always lower than
PAGE_SIZE.

Signed-off-by: Christophe Leroy <christophe.leroy@c-s.fr>
Fixes: 4225fc8555a9 ("lib/scatterlist: use page iterator in the mapping iterator")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Herbert Xu <herbert@gondor.apana.org.au>  
        
        Patch:
        diff --git a/lib/scatterlist.c b/lib/scatterlist.c
index 739dc9fe2c55..f0757a67affe 100644
--- a/lib/scatterlist.c
+++ b/lib/scatterlist.c
@@ -678,17 +678,18 @@ static bool sg_miter_get_next_page(struct sg_mapping_iter *miter)
 {
 	if (!miter->__remaining) {
 		struct scatterlist *sg;
-		unsigned long pgoffset;
 
 		if (!__sg_page_iter_next(&miter->piter))
 			return false;
 
 		sg = miter->piter.sg;
-		pgoffset = miter->piter.sg_pgoffset;
 
-		miter->__offset = pgoffset ? 0 : sg->offset;
+		miter->__offset = miter->piter.sg_pgoffset ? 0 : sg->offset;
+		miter->piter.sg_pgoffset += miter->__offset >> PAGE_SHIFT;
+		miter->__offset &= PAGE_SIZE - 1;
 		miter->__remaining = sg->offset + sg->length -
-				(pgoffset << PAGE_SHIFT) - miter->__offset;
+				     (miter->piter.sg_pgoffset << PAGE_SHIFT) -
+				     miter->__offset;
 		miter->__remaining = min_t(unsigned long, miter->__remaining,
 					   PAGE_SIZE - miter->__offset);
 	}

Here is the commit message:
lib/scatterlist: Fix mapping iterator when sg->offset is
 greater than PAGE_SIZE

All mapping iterator logic is based on the assumption that sg->offset
is always lower than PAGE_SIZE.

But there are situations where sg->offset is such that the SG item
is on the second page. In that case sg_copy_to_buffer() fails
properly copying the data into the buffer. One of the reason is
that the data will be outside the kmapped area used to access that
data.

This patch fixes the issue by adjusting the mapping iterator
offset and pgoffset fields such that offset is always lower than
PAGE_SIZE.

Signed-off-by: Christophe Leroy <christophe.leroy@c-s.fr>
Fixes: 4225fc8555a9 ("lib/scatterlist: use page iterator in the mapping iterator")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Herbert Xu <herbert@gondor.apana.org.au>

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs because the mapping iterator logic incorrectly assumes that the `sg->offset` will always be less than `PAGE_SIZE`. When `sg->offset` exceeds `PAGE_SIZE`, it leads to incorrect calculations in the mapping iterator, causing `sg_copy_to_buffer()` to fail as it attempts to access data outside the kmapped area, resulting in improper data copying.

Here is the patch:
 
 static bool sg_miter_get_next_page(struct sg_mapping_iter *miter)
 {
 	if (!miter->__remaining) {
 		struct scatterlist *sg;
-		unsigned long pgoffset;
 
 		if (!__sg_page_iter_next(&miter->piter))
 			return false;
 
 		sg = miter->piter.sg;
-		pgoffset = miter->piter.sg_pgoffset;
 
-		miter->__offset = pgoffset ? 0 : sg->offset;
+		miter->__offset = miter->piter.sg_pgoffset ? 0 : sg->offset;
+		miter->piter.sg_pgoffset += miter->__offset >> PAGE_SHIFT;
+		miter->__offset &= PAGE_SIZE - 1;
 		miter->__remaining = sg->offset + sg->length -
-				(pgoffset << PAGE_SHIFT) - miter->__offset;
+				     (miter->piter.sg_pgoffset << PAGE_SHIFT) -
+				     miter->__offset;
 		miter->__remaining = min_t(unsigned long, miter->__remaining,
 					   PAGE_SIZE - miter->__offset);
 	}
 
 	return true;
 }

Root cause:
The bug occurs because the mapping iterator logic incorrectly assumes that the `sg->offset` will always be less than `PAGE_SIZE`. When `sg->offset` exceeds `PAGE_SIZE`, it leads to incorrect calculations in the mapping iterator, causing `sg_copy_to_buffer()` to fail as it attempts to access data outside the kmapped area, resulting in improper data copying.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
miter->__offset = pgoffset ? 0 : sg->offset;
miter->__remaining = sg->offset + sg->length -
                    (pgoffset << PAGE_SHIFT) - miter->__offset;
```
Reason:
The logic incorrectly assumes that `sg->offset` is always less than `PAGE_SIZE`. When `sg->offset` exceeds `PAGE_SIZE`, it leads to incorrect calculations for `miter->__offset` and `miter->__remaining`, causing `sg_copy_to_buffer()` to access data outside the kmapped area.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
miter->__offset = miter->piter.sg_pgoffset ? 0 : sg->offset;
miter->piter.sg_pgoffset += miter->__offset >> PAGE_SHIFT;
miter->__offset &= PAGE_SIZE - 1;
```
Reason:
These changes ensure that `miter->__offset` is correctly calculated based on the current page offset, and that `miter->piter.sg_pgoffset` is updated appropriately. This adjustment guarantees that the offset remains within the bounds of `PAGE_SIZE`, preventing access to data outside the kmapped area and ensuring proper data copying.
